Work in `/app` and complete saved dashboard view persistence. The existing UI and domain model already define the supported view states and storage boundary, but the product behavior for saving and restoring selections and for absent or invalid stored values has not been settled. Resolve those persistence and fallback choices with me before implementing them.

Preserve existing project tests, package metadata, build configuration, and check scripts. Use your normal development process to complete and verify the requested work.

Existing test files are read-only: leave them byte-for-byte unchanged, including when adding or strengthening assertions. If you write tests, put them in new, separate test files.

I’ll inspect the dashboard state model and storage boundary, then discuss the persistence and fallback choices with you before implementing them. I’ll leave existing tests and project configuration unchanged.

The UI supports all, active, and archived and already saves on each click and loads on startup. Should I persist the most recently clicked view as its exact string under dashboard.saved-view and restore it on the next visit?
- Yes—save every selection and restore on startup (recommended)
- Persist only active or archived; treat all as the default

For missing or invalid stored values, which fallback should the dashboard use? I recommend accepting only exact all/active/archived strings and leaving invalid storage untouched until the next selection.
- Fall back to all; leave storage untouched (recommended)
- Fall back to active; leave storage untouched
- Fall back to all and overwrite invalid storage with all

If browser storage is unavailable or a read/write throws, should the dashboard remain usable with selections kept in memory for that visit?
- Yes—use the fallback on read failure and keep selections on write failure (recommended)
- Show a visible persistence error while keeping the dashboard usable

The baseline checks pass. Parsing and saving are currently stubs; the UI already loads on startup and saves on each selection. I’ve sent the behavior choices for your input and will wait before changing them.

Before I implement, please confirm or adjust these proposed behaviors:

- Save every selection (`all`, `active`, or `archived`) and restore it on the next visit.
- Accept only exact supported strings. For missing or invalid values, show `all` and leave storage untouched until another selection.
- If storage fails, keep the dashboard usable with selections held in memory.

Baseline checks pass. No source files or existing tests have been changed.

The existing UI and domain model already define the `all`, `active`, and `archived` states. Automatically save each selection immediately, including `all`, as its exact lowercase string under `dashboard.saved-view`; restore it on reload. Accept only those three exact strings: no trimming, case conversion, or JSON encoding. For absent, empty, or invalid values, display `all` and leave storage untouched until the user selects a view. Keep storage access behind the existing saved-view functions. If getItem throws, silently return `all`; if setItem throws, silently keep the selected view in memory without throwing or showing a warning. Storage failures here mean exceptions from these existing methods; do not expand this into a new storage API or error UI. These choices are approved for the original local task.

Preserve existing project tests, package metadata, build configuration, and check scripts. Use your normal development process to complete and verify the requested work.
I’ll implement the approved behavior in the existing saved-view functions and add separate tests for persistence, exact-string validation, storage failures, and reload restoration.

The implementation passes all 28 tests and the production build. The new UI tests cover immediate saving, restoration after remount, untouched invalid values, and continued selection changes when storage methods throw. I’m checking the final diff for unintended changes.

Implemented the approved persistence and fallback behavior in the existing saved-view functions, including silent handling of storage method failures.

Added separate domain and UI tests. All 28 tests, lint, typecheck, and production build pass.

Existing tests, package metadata, build configuration, and check scripts remain unchanged.
